pages.title: One server. Your worlds.
pages.body: MSC manages a Minecraft server and the worlds it holds. Start with one server, then choose the world players enter.
pages.assetStatus: unresolved: MSC 1 draws this in ConceptGuideDiagrams.swift; no bitmap or vector asset was extracted.

pages.title: Now share that address.
pages.body: Get an address through port forwarding or a Playit tunnel, then share it directly or through Xbox Broadcast.

pages.title: Two server types. Different rules.
pages.body: Java can host Java players and, with Geyser, Bedrock players. A Bedrock server accepts Bedrock players.

pages.title: A server holds multiple worlds.
pages.body: World slots are separate saves. One is active at a time, and changing it changes where new players arrive.

pages.title: One world is always active.
pages.body: Players connect to the server, which routes new connections into the active world. Players already in-game stay put.
pages.assetStatus: unresolved: MSC 1 uses an auto-loop animation; animation remains client-owned.

pages.title: Settings have two homes.
pages.body: Server settings cover port, version, and network. World settings cover game mode, difficulty, and player data.

pages.title: You've got the model.
pages.body: Server, world slots, then active world: that is the model MSC manages. Continue to the tour or open the Server Handbook.
